chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The chief of deeds is fairness with people from yourself, and equalizing with the brother for the sake of Allah, and remembering Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon every state.'

key_terms.مُوَاسَاةُ الْأَخِ فِي اللَّهِ: Equalizing/solidarity with the brother for the sake of God

ai.seo_question: What are the three chief deeds in Shia Islam according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi elevates 'insaf' (fairness/justice) as the master of all deeds, linking self-accountability directly to communal solidarity and perpetual dhikr. It reflects the Imami emphasis on integrating inner spiritual consciousness with outward social ethics, positioning the believer's relationship with God and the community as inseparable pillars of faith.
